question: Does vitamin D3 raise 25(OH)D more than D2?
pooled_effect: 10.39 nmol/L (40%) lower total 25(OH)D with D2
notes: Difference lost significance in participants with BMI above 25

question: Does dietary fat improve vitamin D3 absorption?
outcome: Peak plasma vitamin D3 12 h after a 50 000 IU dose
pooled_effect: 32% greater peak plasma D3 with a fat-containing meal
notes: A companion trial found higher absorption without higher 25(OH)D at 90 days

question: Is MK-7 better absorbed than MK-4?
pooled_effect: Serum MK-4 undetectable after 420 mcg; MK-7 detectable to 48 h
notes: MK-4 is cleared within about an hour and does not accumulate on repeated dosing

question: How long does MK-7 circulate?
outcome: Elimination half-life and bioavailability relative to K1
pooled_effect: Half-life 68-72 h versus 1-2 h for K1; AUC 2.5x at 24 h and 6x at 96 h
notes: Long half-life is the basis for once-daily MK-7 dosing

question: What 25(OH)D level meets population needs?
studies_participants: Systematic review of observational and trial data
pooled_effect: 20 ng/mL (50 nmol/L) meets the needs of about 97.5% of the population
notes: The IOM explicitly declined to endorse 30 ng/mL as a requirement

question: Should healthy people have 25(OH)D tested?
population: General population including adults over 75 and pregnant people
pooled_effect: Suggests against routine screening and against follow-up testing to guide dosing
notes: The 2024 guideline replaced the 2011 guideline that endorsed a 30 ng/mL target

question: How common is low vitamin D status?
population: US population aged 1 year and older
pooled_effect: At risk of inadequacy fell from 18.8% to 15.6%; levels above 125 nmol/L rose from 2.2% to 7.6%
notes: High status is becoming more common as supplement use increases

question: Does vitamin D3 alone prevent fractures in replete adults?
population: Adults 50 and older not selected for deficiency or osteoporosis
pooled_effect: Total fractures HR 0.98; hip fractures HR 1.01
notes: No effect modification by baseline 25(OH)D including levels below 12 ng/mL

question: Does calcium plus vitamin D prevent hip fracture?
pooled_effect: RR 0.84 with calcium plus vitamin D
notes: Benefit concentrated in institutionalised and deficient populations; vitamin D alone did not reduce fracture

question: Do calcium and vitamin D prevent fractures overall?
pooled_effect: Any fracture RR 0.91 with combined supplementation; vitamin D alone RR 1.00
notes: Absolute reductions were below thresholds considered clinically meaningful

question: What dose of vitamin D affects falls?
pooled_effect: 800-1000 IU/day RR 0.85; doses above 1000 IU/day increased falls
notes: Intermittent dosing showed no preventive effect

question: Can high-dose intermittent vitamin D cause harm?
pooled_effect: Annual 500 000 IU increased falls (IRR 1.15) and fractures (IRR 1.26)
notes: Harm appeared within the first three months

question: Does MK-7 slow postmenopausal bone loss?
pooled_effect: Less decline in lumbar spine and femoral neck BMD and BMC with MK-7 180 mcg/day
notes: Not replicated in a larger trial that gave vitamin D and calcium to both arms

question: Does MK-7 add bone benefit on top of vitamin D and calcium?
pooled_effect: No between-group difference in aBMD at any site with MK-7 375 mcg/day
notes: Carboxylation of osteocalcin improved but bone density did not

question: Does low-dose K2 help bone in Chinese adults?
pooled_effect: Less femoral neck bone loss at 90 mcg/day in postmenopausal women only
notes: Adding calcium and vitamin D3 produced no additional effect

question: Does vitamin K reduce clinical fractures?
pooled_effect: OR 0.72; 0.76 when restricted to low risk of bias trials
notes: No difference in vertebral fractures; BMD differences were small and not robust

question: Does high-dose MK-4 prevent fractures in osteoporosis?
pooled_effect: Fewer clinical fractures with menatetrenone 45 mg/day; lumbar BMD maintained
notes: Open-label design and Japanese regulatory context limit generalisation

question: Does K2 activate vitamin K-dependent proteins?
population: Adults with and without vascular disease
pooled_effect: dp-ucMGP falls substantially and consistently
notes: This is a mechanism marker not a clinical outcome

question: Does vitamin K slow coronary calcification?
pooled_effect: MD -17.37 Agatston units with vitamin K supplementation
notes: Driven by small trials; not designed to detect clinical events

question: Does MK-7 plus D slow aortic valve calcification?
population: Men aged 65-74 with score above 300 AU
pooled_effect: Mean difference 17 AU (not significant)
notes: dp-ucMGP fell significantly while calcification progressed equally

question: Does MK-7 plus D help high-risk coronary calcification?
population: Men with CAC at least 400 AU
pooled_effect: CAC rose 288 versus 380 AU in the high-CAC subgroup
notes: Primary endpoint was neutral; subgroup finding is hypothesis-generating

question: Does K2 help vascular calcification in dialysis?
pooled_effect: No difference in CAC (relative mean difference 0.85)
notes: No difference in arterial stiffness or major events

question: Does vitamin D prevent acute respiratory infection?
outcome: Proportion with at least one ARI
pooled_effect: OR 0.88; 0.81 with daily or weekly dosing without bolus
notes: Stronger where baseline 25(OH)D was below 25 nmol/L

question: Does the respiratory infection benefit replicate?
pooled_effect: OR 0.94 (p=0.057) with no subgroup effect modification
notes: Funnel plot asymmetry suggested publication bias

question: Does vitamin D prevent autoimmune disease?
pooled_effect: HR 0.78 during 5.3 years; HR 0.98 at 7 years
notes: Benefit was not sustained after supplementation stopped

question: Does vitamin D prevent cardiovascular events?
notes: No signal in the primary analysis

question: Does monthly vitamin D affect cardiovascular events?
notes: Apparent benefit in participants taking cardiovascular drugs at baseline

question: Does vitamin D prevent cancer?
notes: No reduction in the primary analysis

question: Does vitamin D reduce cancer mortality?
pooled_effect: RR 0.87 overall; effect attributable to daily dosing
notes: Incidence was not reduced; the benefit is on mortality and is small in absolute terms

question: Does vitamin D reduce all-cause mortality?
notes: Cancer death RR 0.85 was the only significant component

question: Is there a mortality benefit after age 75?
pooled_effect: Very small reduction with daily low-dose supplementation
notes: This is the basis for the 2024 recommendation in adults over 75

question: Does vitamin D prevent diabetes in prediabetes?
notes: Not significant in the intention-to-treat analysis

question: Does vitamin D slow progression from prediabetes?
pooled_effect: 15% lower risk of progression; 30% more regression to normal glucose regulation
notes: Pooled analysis was more powerful than any single trial

question: Is daily dosing better than bolus dosing?
studies_participants: Daily and weekly dosing versus bolus
pooled_effect: Daily low-dose preferred; bolus dosing showed no benefit and possible falls harm
notes: Reflected in the 2024 Endocrine Society technical remarks

question: What happens at 4000 and 10 000 IU daily?
pooled_effect: Mild hypercalcemia in 3% at 4000 IU and 9% at 10 000 IU versus 0% at 400 IU
notes: All cases resolved on repeat testing; no clinical adverse event imbalance

question: Are doses near the upper limit safe?
population: Adults in trials lasting 6 months or more
pooled_effect: Hypercalcemia RR 2.21; falls RR 1.25; hospitalization RR 1.16
notes: Kidney stones and hypercalciuria did not differ significantly

question: Does high-dose vitamin D cause kidney stones?
pooled_effect: HR 0.90 for a first stone event
notes: Monthly 100 000 IU produced no hypercalcemia

question: Does vitamin D plus calcium increase stone risk?
evidence_type: Government fact sheet synthesis of trial data
pooled_effect: Calcium taken with vitamin D may increase risk of some adverse effects
notes: The signal is attributed to calcium loading rather than vitamin D itself

question: Does MK-7 destabilise warfarin-type anticoagulation?
pooled_effect: MK-7 45 mcg/day lowered INR by 20-37%; 10-20 mcg judged clinically relevant in some
notes: Authors conclude MK-7 supplements should be avoided during vitamin K antagonist therapy

question: Is there a safe upper limit for MK-7?
population: Adults not taking vitamin K antagonists
studies_participants: Clinical trials up to 999 mcg/day and 45 mg MK-4
pooled_effect: No serious adverse effects; no UL established; CRN sets a habitually observed intake of 375 mcg/day
notes: Explicitly does not apply to people taking vitamin K antagonists

question: At what 25(OH)D level does toxicity appear?
pooled_effect: Toxicity is rare below 150 ng/mL (375 nmol/L)
notes: Sustained intakes above 10 000 IU/day are the usual cause

question: Do vitamin D products match their labels?
pooled_effect: Two products contained up to twice the labelled vitamin D
notes: Both exceeded the tolerable upper intake level at the labelled serving

question: How variable is vitamin D pill potency?
pooled_effect: Range 52% to 135% of expected dose; the USP-verified manufacturer measured 101.7%
notes: Two-thirds of bottles met USP content standards on average

question: Is MK-7 in supplements the active all-trans form?
pooled_effect: all-trans content often below label; cis and trans MK-6 and MK-7 impurities 70.9-218.7 mcg per unit
notes: Tablets tended to under-deliver and oil capsules to over-deliver

question: Do vitamin K products match their labels?
pooled_effect: One product contained 80.8% of its MK-7 claim; one combination contained far more vitamin D than listed
notes: Most vitamin K products met their claims

question: Do combined D3 and K2 products meet specifications?
pooled_effect: Significant deviations from labelled content for both vitamins
notes: Authors concluded quality control was insufficient for most products tested

question: Does adding K2 to D3 improve bone density?
pooled_effect: Combined D3 and MK-4 increased BMD more than either alone
notes: Used alfacalcidol rather than cholecalciferol; not a retail D3 product

question: Does K2 add benefit when calcium and D3 are adequate?
pooled_effect: No additional effect from combining K2 with calcium and D3
notes: Direct test of the marketing claim in a low-dose design

question: Does K2 improve bone turnover on top of D3 and calcium?
pooled_effect: Carboxylation improved but BMD and microarchitecture did not
notes: Best-powered test of the combination hypothesis for bone density
